text:
Nina: brain fried, need a 20-min bedtime playlist + a one-sentence pitch for 'short cozy books' for my partner.
Rohit: for 20 min chill: low-fi + ambient piano. My go-to: `Tycho - Awake (first 20 mins)` mixed with `Ólafur Arnalds` piano tracks.
Bea: Book rec: 'The Little Paris Bookshop' 9-ish pages? Romance-y, gentle. Pitch: 'A small, bookish balm for messy hearts.'
Tom: If you want micro-memoirs: try 'On Looking' by Alexandra Horowitz (short essays). Also recommend a dumb comedy: 'Parks and Rec' for brain-melting comfort. :tada:
Evelyn: Tiny poll: what vibe? React: calm = :zzz:, nerdy = :book:, silly = :joy:  
Rohit: :zzz:
Bea: :book:
Tom: :joy:
Nina: most votes calm. dropping a tiny playlist in case anyone wants it: 3 tracks, mellow, under 22 minutes.
Nina: 1) Hammock - Turn Away And Return 2) Explosions in the Sky - Your Hand in Mine (edit) 3) Julianna Barwick - The Harbinger.
Bot-Music: automated note: you can open `https://open.spotify.com/playlist/example` to preview (mock link).
Evelyn: one-line pitch for Little Paris Bookshop: 'A traveling bookseller mends strangers' lives one story at a time.'
Bea: alternative cozy: 'The Comforts of Home' (collection of short essays) - good between meetings.
Tom: movie rec for tonight if anyone's curious: 'The Grand Budapest Hotel'  visual candy and quick enough.
Nina: thanks y'all. last thing: anyone read anything <= 150 pages that's actually funny? looking for laugh-before-bed.
Rohit: 'The Mezzanine' by Nicholson Baker is short and quietly absurd.
Bea: 'Slaughterhouse-Five' is short and great but not exactly light. still a classic.
Tom: GIF: :laughing_cat: (useful)
Nina: perfect. signing off to make chamomile and read. will report if I laugh out loud. :wave:
